r.정치 구도: A directly elected president appoints the premier, and the Legislative Yuan handles laws and the budget. Democratization followed the lifting of martial law in 1987, and presidents have been directly elected since 1996. The Democratic Progressive Party, which keeps China at a distance, and the Kuomintang, which favors dialogue with China, are the main rivals, and third parties such as the Taiwan People's Party have grown. When the president and the legislative majority differ, they clash hard over budgets and bills. A growing number of people identify themselves as 'Taiwanese'.

t.why: Its official name is the Republic of China. The Kuomintang government moved there after the Chinese civil war in 1949, and it left the UN when a 1971 General Assembly resolution gave China's seat to the People's Republic of China. As of 2026 only 12 countries formally recognize it, mostly small states in Latin America and the Pacific; 10 have switched recognition to China since 2016 alone. So even how to use the name 'Taiwan' becomes a diplomatic issue. It competes in the Olympics and APEC as 'Chinese Taipei', and belongs to the World Trade Organization as a 'separate customs territory' covering Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu. In countries without formal ties, it keeps representative offices with names such as 'Taipei Economic and Cultural Office' instead of embassies. When Lithuania allowed the name 'Taiwanese Representative Office' in 2021, China downgraded diplomatic relations with Lithuania and blocked its trade. It attended the World Health Assembly as an observer from 2009 to 2016 but has not been invited since. Its formal ties are narrow, but because it leads the world in advanced chipmaking, its unofficial exchanges with the United States, Japan and Europe run very deep.
t.rel: China regards Taiwan as its territory and aims for unification. Only a dozen or so countries recognize it, but it has deep unofficial ties with the United States, Japan and others, and US law commits the United States to help Taiwan maintain its ability to defend itself.
t.korea: Korea cut official diplomatic ties with Taiwan when it established relations with China in 1992, and since the following year the two have dealt through representative offices: the Taipei Mission in Korea and the Korean Mission in Taipei. They compete in chips while buying parts and equipment from each other. Both face similar dilemmas between China and the United States, so they watch each other's responses. Tourism is brisk, and Korean dramas and music are very popular in Taiwan.
t.know: Taipei's National Palace Museum holds hundreds of thousands of artifacts moved from Beijing's Forbidden City during the Chinese civil war.
etext: Taiwanese companies handle most of the world's most advanced chip contract manufacturing. Chips designed by companies such as Apple and Nvidia are made in Taiwanese fabs. Its chip packaging and design firms are strong too.
Taiwanese companies assemble most of the servers that go into AI data centers. Its supply chains for electronic parts and computer peripherals are dense.
The economy is heavily concentrated in chips, and military tension with China is a constant risk. At US urging, it is building plants abroad too.
